table.name: badges
table.purpose: Badge awards on a Stack Exchange-style Q&A site: one row per badge granted to a user. The surrounding tables (users, posts, votes, comments, tags, postHistory, postLinks) are exactly the Stack Exchange data-dump schema, and the badge names (Student, Supporter, Editor, Scholar, Teacher, Autobiographer, Analytical) are canonical Stack Exchange badges. The tag-like names (correlation, nonparametric, modeling, pca) indicate tag badges for a statistics-oriented site (consistent with Cross Validated, stats.stackexchange.com). A user can earn the same badge multiple times; each award is its own row. Note the schema lacks the Class/TagBased columns of the official dump, so badge class must be inferred from the name if needed.

Date.name: awarded_at
Date.description: Timestamp (second precision) at which the badge was awarded to the user. Range 2010-07-19 to 2014-09-14, matching the site's lifetime in the dump. The single spike at 2014-07-02 16:05:34 (899 rows) reflects a bulk award/recalculation event on that date, not a different meaning; all other values are individually spread in time.

Id.name: badge_award_id
Id.description: Surrogate primary key uniquely identifying one badge-award row (1..92240, no gaps in distinctness). It identifies the award event, not the badge type (the type is Name) nor the user. The accepted joins from postLinks.LinkTypeId and posts.PostTypeId are coincidental numeric matches: those columns hold small type codes (roughly 1-3), which trivially match low badge Ids; they are not real relationships and should be ignored.

Name.name: badge_name
Name.description: Name of the badge awarded. 153 distinct values of two kinds: standard Stack Exchange achievement badges (Student, Supporter, Editor, Scholar, Teacher, Autobiographer, Analytical, ...) and tag badges named after the site's tags for sustained contributions in that topic (correlation, nonparametric, modeling, pca, ...). The tag-badge names double as entries in the tags table. This is the badge type, not a person name.

UserId.name: user_id
UserId.description: Foreign key to users.Id: the user who received this badge. Many-to-one (79,851 awards across 25,078 users; the most-decorated user, Id 919, holds 456 badges). No nulls, so every award is tied to a known user.

table.name: comments
table.purpose: One row per comment on a Stack Exchange-style Q&A site. Comments are short remarks attached to posts (questions or answers) via PostId, written by users, with a creation timestamp, body text, and an upvote score. The content (mentions of @whuber, @probabilityislogic, Harrell's 'RMS' book, regression/time-series/tree topics) strongly suggests a statistics Q&A site, likely Cross Validated (stats.stackexchange.com).

CreationDate.name: comment_creation_timestamp
CreationDate.description: Date and time the comment was posted. Values span 2009-02-02 to 2014-09-14 and are nearly unique per row (uniqueness 0.999), consistent with per-comment creation times on an active site.

Id.name: comment_id
Id.description: Primary key: unique identifier of the comment (174,285 distinct values = row count). The 'referenced_by' joins to postHistory.PostId, postLinks.LinkTypeId, posts.PostTypeId and posts.ParentId are numeric coincidences (post ids and small type codes), not genuine references to comments.

PostId.name: post_id
PostId.description: Foreign key to posts.Id: the question or answer the comment was posted on. Many comments per post (top post has 45; 53,416 distinct posts). The join to postHistory.Id is coincidental; the real target is posts.Id.

Score.name: upvote_count
Score.description: Upvote score of the comment. Non-negative (min 0, max 90) and heavily skewed: ~77% of comments have score 0, consistent with Stack Exchange comment scores, which count upvotes only (comments cannot be downvoted).

Text.name: comment_body
Text.description: Body text of the comment. Free text, nearly unique per row; typical Q&A comment content such as @username replies, thanks, clarifying questions, and moderation notes ('While this link may answer the question, it is better to include the essential parts...').

UserDisplayName.name: author_display_name
UserDisplayName.description: Display name of the comment author, populated only when the author's user account no longer exists: null in 98.4% of rows, exactly complementing UserId's 1.6% null rate. Values like 'user10525' match Stack Exchange's anonymized deleted-account naming; others are real names (e.g. 'Mariano Suárez-Alvarez').

UserId.name: author_user_id
UserId.description: Foreign key to users.Id: the user who wrote the comment. Null in 1.6% of rows, precisely where UserDisplayName is filled (deleted accounts). 13,647 distinct commenters; the most prolific (Id 919) wrote 13,220 comments.

table.name: postHistory
table.purpose: One row per post-history event on a Stack Exchange-style Q&A site — the standard 'PostHistory' table of a Stack Exchange data dump (sibling tables posts, users, comments, votes, badges, tags, postLinks; content such as tags '<regression>', '<r>', '<probability>' and the moderator 'whuber' indicate the site is Cross Validated, stats.stackexchange.com). Each row records a single event in a post's life: initial title/body/tags at creation, later edits and rollbacks, closure, deletion, migration, etc. The rows sharing a PostId, grouped by RevisionGUID, reconstruct a post's full revision and moderation history.

Comment.name: Comment
Comment.description: Free-text revision comment / edit summary attached to the event; empty string (181,184 rows, ~60%) means no comment. Values are either auto-generated by the site's edit UI ('edited title', 'edited tags', 'edited body', 'added 1 characters in body', 'removed signature and greetings'), suggested-edit audit lines ('Proposed by 26080 approved by 21054, -1 edit id of 3592'), or free-form reasons typed by editors ('presentation needed improvement!').

CreationDate.name: CreationDate
CreationDate.description: Timestamp (YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS) when the history event occurred, spanning 2009-02-02 (site launch) to 2014-09-14 (dump date). Tight clusters such as 81 rows at 2012-02-22 19:46:04 reflect bulk/batched operations (e.g. a mass retag or data backfill) rather than individual user actions.

Id.name: Id
Id.description: Primary key of postHistory: unique identifier (1–386,848) of one history-event row. The 'referenced_by' joins reported for it (comments.PostId, posts.ParentId, posts.PostTypeId, postLinks.LinkTypeId, votes.VoteTypeId) are numeric coincidences — those columns point at posts.Id or small type codes, not at this table.

PostHistoryTypeId.name: PostHistoryTypeId
PostHistoryTypeId.description: Code identifying the kind of history event (Stack Exchange's PostHistoryTypeId); 25 distinct codes in the range 1–38. Corroborated mapping: 1=Initial Title, 2=Initial Body, 3=Initial Tags, 4=Edit Title, 5=Edit Body, 6=Edit Tags, 7/8/9=Rollback Title/Body/Tags, 10=Post Closed, 11=Post Reopened, 12=Post Deleted, 13=Post Undeleted, 14/15=Post Locked/Unlocked, 16=Community Owned; codes 17–38 cover migration, merging, protection, post notices, tweeting/mentioning and spam/offensive/flag events per the standard Stack Exchange list (exact labels for these rarer codes are not independently verifiable from this table alone). Evidence: type 2 occurs 91,974 times vs 91,976 distinct PostIds (every post has exactly one initial-body row); types 1 (42,909) and 3 (42,921) match the number of questions — the only posts with title/tags; type 5 is the most frequent edit, matching the 'edited body' comments; close events carry a JSON voter list in Text. The reported join to posts.Id is spurious — these are small type codes, not post ids.

PostId.name: PostId
PostId.description: Id of the post this event applies to (references posts.Id). 91,976 distinct posts with up to 32 events each; the rows sharing a PostId form that post's history. The reported join to comments.Id is a numeric coincidence.

RevisionGUID.name: RevisionGUID
RevisionGUID.description: UUID grouping the history rows that belong to one logical revision: a question's creation writes three rows (initial title, body, tags) sharing one GUID, and a single edit touching title+body+tags likewise shares one GUID — hence only 193,951 distinct GUIDs for 303,155 rows (uniqueness 0.64). The all-zero GUID (169 rows) is a placeholder for events that are not revisions (e.g. close/reopen/lock).

Text.name: Text
Text.description: The content written by the event: the title text for title events, the body markdown for body events, the tag string for tag events (e.g. '<regression><r>', '<probability>', '<reference-request>'), and a JSON record of the close/reopen voters for moderation events (e.g. '{"Voters":[{"Id":919,"DisplayName":"whuber"}]}'). Empty string (24,482 rows) for events that carry no content (lock, protect, migrate, etc.).

UserDisplayName.name: UserDisplayName
UserDisplayName.description: Display name of the user who caused the event, populated only when the account cannot be referenced through UserId (deleted or never-registered users) — hence the anonymized 'userNNNNN' forms; empty string in 298,316 of 303,155 rows.

UserId.name: UserId
UserId.description: Id of the user who performed the event (references users.Id). -1 (the minimum) is the Community/system account in Stack Exchange dumps; NULL in ~7% of rows when the acting user is unknown or deleted, in which case UserDisplayName may carry the name instead. The most frequent ids (7290, 919, 805, 88, 930) are the site's most active editors; 919 is the moderator 'whuber' (see the voter JSON in Text).

table.name: postLinks (post-to-post relationship table)
table.purpose: Each row records one directed link between two posts in a Stack Exchange-style Q&A database (companion tables: posts, users, votes, comments, badges, tags, postHistory). PostId is the post the link is attached to, RelatedPostId is the post it points to, and LinkTypeId classifies the relationship as an ordinary 'linked/related' association (1) or a duplicate-question relationship (3). This is the PostLinks table of the standard Stack Exchange data dump.

CreationDate.name: Link creation timestamp
CreationDate.description: Timestamp (stored as text, 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS') of when the link record was created; never null; spans 2010-07-21 to 2014-09-13, matching the site's activity period. ~85% of values are distinct; the modal value 2013-02-18 03:03:17 occurs 234 times, indicating a bulk backfill/import of links at that moment rather than organic activity. Not used as a join key.

Id.name: Post link ID (surrogate primary key)
Id.description: Unique BIGINT identifying the link row; 11,102 distinct values equal the row count and it is detected as the table's primary key. Values are sparse up to ~3.36M, consistent with a site-wide ID sequence shared across the dump. No other table joins to it.

LinkTypeId.name: Link type code (1 = Linked, 3 = Duplicate)
LinkTypeId.description: Two-valued code distinguishing the kind of post relationship: 1 (10,186 rows, ~92%) and 3 (916 rows, ~8%). In the Stack Exchange schema this is the PostLinkType enum: 1 = Linked (the posts are related, typically auto-created when one post references the other) and 3 = Duplicate (PostId was closed as a duplicate of RelatedPostId). The observed distribution fits: duplicate links are far rarer than ordinary reference links. It is a code, not a foreign key; the accepted joins to badges.Id / comments.Id / postHistory.Id are statistical coincidences of small integers matching unrelated ID ranges.

PostId.name: Source post ID (FK to posts.Id)
PostId.description: ID of the post the link belongs to: the post that references the related post, or the question marked as a duplicate of it. Joins to posts.Id (many-to-one). 7,604 distinct values over 11,102 rows, so a post can carry several links (multiple references, or links in both directions). Value range 4-115,360 matches posts.Id.

RelatedPostId.name: Target (related) post ID (FK to posts.Id)
RelatedPostId.description: ID of the post being linked to: the referenced post, or the original question in a duplicate relationship. Joins to posts.Id (many-to-one). 5,177 distinct values; the most frequent targets (post 2492 with 96 inbound links, post 20836 with 93) look like canonical questions that many posts point to, supporting the reading that this is the link target. Range 1-115,163 matches posts.Id.

table.name: posts
table.purpose: All posts (questions, answers, tag wikis) of a Stack Exchange-style Q&A site about statistics (content: regression, hypothesis-testing, R, Stata, 'degrees of freedom', stats.stackexchange.com duplicate links — i.e., Cross Validated), Feb 2009 – Sep 2014. One row per post, with content, authorship, counts, and lifecycle timestamps.

AcceptedAnswerId.name: Accepted answer post ID
AcceptedAnswerId.description: For questions, the posts.Id of the answer the asker accepted as best (self-reference to this table; the profiler missed the join, but values fall inside the Id range and are unique). Null for answers and for questions with no accepted answer; only ~16% of rows are populated, consistent with the question share.

AnswerCount.name: Answer count
AnswerCount.description: Number of answers the question received (0–136). Populated only on questions: non-null share 46.7% exactly matches the PostTypeId=1 share; null on answers and other types.

Body.name: Post body (HTML)
Body.description: Full text content of the post as sanitized HTML (question text, answer text, or tag wiki text). Near-unique per row.

ClosedDate.name: Closed timestamp
ClosedDate.description: Date-time the question was closed (e.g., duplicate, off-topic); null for open questions, answers, and other post types (~1.8% populated). Format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS.

CommentCount.name: Comment count
CommentCount.description: Number of comments on the post (0–45); consistent with the comments table referencing posts via comments.PostId.

CommunityOwnedDate.name: Community wiki conversion timestamp
CommunityOwnedDate.description: Date-time the post was converted to community wiki (no single owner); null for the ~97% of posts that are not community wiki.

CreaionDate.name: Creation timestamp
CreaionDate.description: Date-time the post was created (column name is a misspelling of CreationDate). Populated on every row; spans 2009-02-02 to 2014-09-14.

FavoriteCount.name: Favorite (bookmark) count
FavoriteCount.description: Number of users who favorited/starred the question (0–233). Recorded only for questions and null for all answers; even among questions it is omitted for most rows in this export (0 also appears 885 times), so null does not strictly mean zero favorites.

Id.name: Post ID (primary key)
Id.description: Primary key: unique identifier of the post. Referenced by comments.PostId, postHistory.PostId, votes.PostId, postLinks.PostId/RelatedPostId, and (one-to-one) tags.ExcerptPostId and tags.WikiPostId for tag wiki posts.

LasActivityDate.name: Last activity timestamp
LasActivityDate.description: Date-time of the most recent activity on the post (edit, comment, or new answer). Misspelling of LastActivityDate. Always populated; never earlier than creation.

LastEditDate.name: Last edit timestamp
LastEditDate.description: Date-time of the most recent edit to the post; null if the post was never edited (~51% of rows, matching LastEditorUserId's null rate).

LastEditorDisplayName.name: Last editor display name (orphaned account)
LastEditorDisplayName.description: Display name of the last editor, stored only when that editor no longer has a user account — hence anonymized values like 'user10525' (0.5% populated). Null whenever the editor is a normal user (see LastEditorUserId).

LastEditorUserId.name: Last editor user ID
LastEditorUserId.description: users.Id of the user who made the most recent edit; -1 denotes the community/deleted user; null if the post was never edited.

OwnerDisplayName.name: Owner display name (orphaned account)
OwnerDisplayName.description: Display name of the post's original author, recorded only when the author no longer has a user account (anonymized 'userNNNNN' names, 2.7% populated); otherwise the owner is identified by OwnerUserId.

OwnerUserId.name: Owner user ID
OwnerUserId.description: users.Id of the user who created/owns the post; -1 denotes the community user or a deleted user; null for ~1.5% of rows (owner gone without a preserved display name, e.g., some tag wikis).

ParentId.name: Parent question ID
ParentId.description: For answers (PostTypeId=2), the posts.Id of the question the answer belongs to — a self-reference to this table (the profiler's joins to postHistory.Id/comments.Id are spurious). Null for questions and other types; non-null share 51.9% exactly matches the answer share.

PostTypeId.name: Post type code
PostTypeId.description: Code classifying the post: 1 = question (42,912 rows — exactly the rows with Title/Tags/ViewCount/AnswerCount), 2 = answer (47,755 rows — exactly the rows with ParentId), 4 = tag wiki excerpt and 5 = tag wiki body (639/640 rows, matching the one-to-one joins to tags.ExcerptPostId / tags.WikiPostId), 6 = moderator nomination post (9 rows), 7 = wiki placeholder. Meanings of 6 and 7 follow the standard Stack Exchange coding and are tentative; the profiler-detected joins to badges/comments/postHistory Ids are small-integer coincidences, not real references.

Score.name: Vote score
Score.description: Net score of the post: upvotes minus downvotes (the votes table references posts via votes.PostId). Ranges -19 to +192, median 2.

Tags.name: Question tags
Tags.description: Angle-bracket-delimited tag names applied to the question, e.g. '<regression><r>'; populated only on questions (null rate matches the non-question share). Tag names correspond to entries in the tags table.

Title.name: Question title
Title.description: Title of the question; populated only on questions (null for answers and other post types). Near-unique.

ViewCount.name: View count
ViewCount.description: Number of times the question page was viewed (1 to 175,495); populated only on questions.

table.name: tags
table.purpose: The tag directory of a Stack-Exchange-style Q&A site: one row per tag, giving its label, how many questions carry it, and links to the posts containing its excerpt and wiki descriptions. The tag vocabulary (2sls, ab-test, glmm, overdispersion, rjags, stratification, joint-distribution, polling) indicates a statistics/Q&A site, consistent with a Cross Validated (stats.stackexchange.com) data dump alongside the posts, users, votes, comments, badges, postHistory and postLinks tables.

Count.name: tag usage count
Count.description: Number of questions on the site tagged with this tag. Ranges from 1 to 7244 with a median of 29: most tags are used on a handful of questions while a few are very common. This is the standard 'Count' column of the Stack Exchange Tags table (count of questions carrying the tag).

ExcerptPostId.name: excerpt post id
ExcerptPostId.description: Foreign key to posts.Id pointing at the post that holds the tag's short excerpt (usage summary). Unique per tag (one-to-one with posts) and null for ~42% of tags, i.e. tags that have no excerpt written yet.

Id.name: tag id
Id.description: Primary key of the tags table; unique identifier for each tag. Values run 1-1869 for 1032 rows, so some ids are absent (deleted or merged tags).

TagName.name: tag name
TagName.description: The tag's display label: a unique, lowercase, hyphenated keyword such as 'glmm', 'ab-test', 'stratification' or 'joint-distribution'. One row per tag name.

WikiPostId.name: wiki post id
WikiPostId.description: Foreign key to posts.Id pointing at the post that holds the tag's full wiki (detailed description). Unique per tag (one-to-one with posts) and null for the same ~42% of tags that lack an excerpt. WikiPostId is consistently ExcerptPostId - 1 (e.g. 65333/65334, 62342/62343), showing the wiki and excerpt posts are created together as a consecutive pair.

table.name: users
table.purpose: One row per registered user account on a Stack Exchange-style Q&A site (the companion tables posts, comments, votes, badges, postHistory, postLinks, tags match the standard Stack Exchange data-dump schema). Each row holds the user's public profile fields (display name, about-me, location, website, avatar) plus denormalized per-user site statistics (reputation, votes cast, profile views) and account timestamps. Id -1 represents the system/'Community' user.

AboutMe.name: AboutMe
AboutMe.description:
Free-text 'About me' biography from the user's profile, stored as an HTML fragment (

...

); null for ~77% of users. Recurring placeholder texts ('please delete me', 'merge keep') are account-deletion/merge requests.

AccountId.name: AccountId
AccountId.description: Network-wide account identifier on the parent platform (the Stack Exchange global account id that links the same person across sites), distinct from the site-local Id primary key; unique per row and not joined to any table in this database. -1 denotes the system/Community user.

Age.name: Age
Age.description: Self-reported age of the user in whole years (range 13-94, median ~30); null for ~79% of users who never filled it in.

CreationDate.name: CreationDate
CreationDate.description: Timestamp (stored as text) of when the user account was registered on the site; spans 2010-07-19 to 2014-09-14, i.e. the site's lifetime up to the dump date.

DisplayName.name: DisplayName
DisplayName.description: Public display name shown on the user's profile and attached to their posts/comments; not unique (common first names repeat). Values like 'user34964' are auto-generated anonymous display names.

DownVotes.name: DownVotes
DownVotes.description: Denormalized count of downvotes cast by the user on the site; 0 for ~98% of users, max 1,920.

Id.name: Id
Id.description: Primary key: site-local numeric user id. Referenced by badges.UserId, comments.UserId, postHistory.UserId, posts.OwnerUserId, posts.LastEditorUserId and votes.UserId. Id -1 is the system/'Community' user (used e.g. for community-owned posts and anonymous votes).

LastAccessDate.name: LastAccessDate
LastAccessDate.description: Timestamp (stored as text) of the user's most recent site visit/login ('last seen'); never earlier than CreationDate and capped at the dump date 2014-09-14.

Location.name: Location
Location.description: Free-text, self-reported location from the profile (mostly 'City, Country' strings, occasionally a time zone such as 'UTC -6'); ~71% null.

ProfileImageUrl.name: ProfileImageUrl
ProfileImageUrl.description: URL of the user's avatar/profile image, mostly gravatar.com hash URLs plus some Google/Facebook image URLs; the most frequent value (3,348 rows) is the default blank-gravatar identicon.

Reputation.name: Reputation
Reputation.description: The user's reputation score on the site (Stack Exchange reputation points earned from upvotes, accepted answers, bounties, etc.). Minimum 1; the very common value 101 = 1 starting point + 100 network 'association bonus'.

UpVotes.name: UpVotes
UpVotes.description: Denormalized count of upvotes cast by the user on the site; 0 for ~78% of users, max 11,442.

Views.name: Views
Views.description: Number of times the user's profile page has been viewed; 0 for ~50% of users, max 20,932.

WebsiteUrl.name: WebsiteUrl
WebsiteUrl.description: Self-reported personal website URL from the profile; ~80% null, and the most common values are placeholder junk typed instead of a real URL ('http://none', 'http://None', 'http://N/A', 'http://-').

table.name: Votes
table.purpose: One row per vote cast on a post of a Stack Exchange-style Q&A site (the sibling tables posts, users, comments, badges, tags, postHistory, postLinks are exactly the Stack Exchange data-dump schema). "Vote" is used broadly: upvotes, downvotes, answer acceptance, favorites, bounties and moderation/spam/close events, distinguished by VoteTypeId. The data covers the site's first ~9 months (2010-07-19 to 2011-05-01), with the busiest days falling in the launch week of July 2010.

BountyAmount.name: Bounty amount
BountyAmount.description: Reputation points pledged or awarded as a bounty on the post. Populated on only ~0.3% of rows (117 of 38,930) - i.e. exclusively on the bounty-related votes (Stack Exchange VoteTypeId 8 = bounty start, 9 = bounty close); null for every ordinary vote. Observed values 0, 25, 50, 100, 150, 200 (median 50, max 200), the typical Stack Exchange bounty sizes; the 25 and 0 values plausibly reflect half-auto-awarded and unawarded bounties.

CreationDate.name: Vote date
CreationDate.description: Date the vote was cast, stored as a YYYY-MM-DD string (declared VARCHAR; no time component - all values are midnight). Range 2010-07-19 to 2011-05-01; the highest-volume days (2010-07-19/20/21/27, 300-464 votes) are the site's launch week.

Id.name: Vote ID
Id.description: Surrogate primary key of the vote row: unique across all 38,930 rows, values 1-43,538. The max exceeding the row count implies some vote rows were deleted or excluded from the dump.

PostId.name: Post ID
PostId.description: Foreign key to posts.Id - the question or answer that received the vote (many-to-one: 8,584 distinct posts are voted on, up to 81 votes on a single post).

UserId.name: Voter user ID
UserId.description: Foreign key to users.Id - the user who cast the vote. Null on 91.2% of rows because ordinary votes (up/down/accept) are anonymized in this dump; the ~3,426 non-null rows correspond to the vote types whose voter is public: the 3,365 favorites (VoteTypeId 5) plus roughly 60 bounty votes. The most frequent values (user 253 with 319 votes, user 3911 with 313) are users who favorited/bountied many posts.

VoteTypeId.name: Vote type code
VoteTypeId.description: Categorical code for the kind of vote, following the standard Stack Exchange vote-type encoding; it is an enum, not a foreign key (the accepted joins to posts.Id / postHistory.Id are spurious small-integer matches). The distribution pins the main codes: 2 = upvote (33,323 rows, 85.6%), 5 = favorite (3,365 - matching the non-null UserId count), 1 = accepted answer (1,451), 3 = downvote (444), 16 = post moderated (111). Sample values add 8, 9 and 10: 8 = bounty start and 9 = bounty close/award (the rows that carry BountyAmount), 10 = deletion. Two further distinct codes (10 distinct in total) cannot be identified from this profile alone; per the same encoding the remaining candidates are 4 offensive, 6 close, 7 reopen, 11 undeletion, 12 spam, 13 moderator review.
